title: Alto saxophone
reference_instrument: University of Iowa MIS alto saxophone (maker and model unstated on the page)
summary: Alto saxophone from the measured air column of one Selmer Super Action Series II specimen (McGill CAML's WIAT 0.1.0: 12 bore stations over 1022 mm, 25 holes with their diameters, chimney heights and centres; numbers only, nothing committed), with the fingerings WIAT lists; the earlier stand-in (one straight cone cut to each note's length, no tone holes) is replaced on C4, E3 and F3, and Ab4 and E5, which the stand-in could not play, have pages. The source does not print the serial (438024 is probable), the method or the uncertainty, flags its own bell as needing more precise equipment, differs from Scavone's 1997 data on the same serial by 8 to 40 mm, puts holes 16 and 17 at one station and overlaps holes 2 and 3, and gives no azimuths; the elbow is laid straight on the pages without the printed bow row (WIAT's comment: about 20 cents) and the key rise h_pad is a typed 2 mm that the card does not use. The reed opening, width and area, the lay profile, the tongue contact row, the reed-noise law, the clarinet's bore-air profile scaled to this bore, the 0.025 m reed channel length with van Zon et al.'s separated-jet law, and, on the pages without the printed mouthpiece row, the mouthpiece push (solved once on the old stand-in's C4) are the earlier pages' rows, borrowed and not tuned after the read. C4, E3 and F3 are blown at 2785, 2745 and 3040 Pa, the new Ab4 and E5 at C4's 2785 Pa (a stated choice). The open-hole interaction is TMMI's with the monopole mutual impedance replaced by its baffled-piston large-distance form: the monopole load was not passive at 575, 551, 435, 512 and 622 of 941 frequencies on the five fingerings, the piston form is passive at all 941 on all five and its coupling error against the exact pair resistance is at most 4.5e-2 (mean 1.6e-3) on C4's geometry; the receipts list no fallback frequency. Played pitch against equal temperament: C4 +18 c, E3 +14 c, F3 +60 c (these three pages carry the player's tract and are read with the autocorrelation reader on 1.0 to 2.3 s, the earlier values with the harmonic product spectrum), Ab4 +9 c; E5's periodicity is an octave below its note (323.46 Hz, E4 -33 c) with the strongest line at 647.00 Hz (E5 -32 c); on the E5 page that carries the player's tract rows (autocorrelation reader) it is 302.22 Hz (-150.3 c from E4, a weak periodicity) with the strongest line at 604.44 Hz (E5 -150.3 c). The loose count is 12 of 15 on C4, 6 of 14 on E3, 7 of 14 on F3, 8 of 14 on Ab4, 5 of 14 on E5 (the pages they replaced: 9, 6, 6, 7, 6; the tract pages of C4 and F3 replaced pages that counted 10 of 15 and 6 of 14). The receiver's grid latency is removed from every clip. The engine's passive impedance from the neck plane agrees with the same specimen's measured maxima at 22 of 27 maxima within 100 cents, as written, below 915 Hz only. Printed rows of 2026-11-09: Nederveen's printed first-order correction of the bow (the apparent phase velocity of a bent pipe, B = 0.60 to 0.69, in place of the straight laying that WIAT puts at about 20 cents) and a mouthpiece cylinder of radius 6.25 mm and length 50.35 mm (6.179 cm3) that is DERIVED here and is not a WIAT statement: Nederveen's rule that the equivalent mouthpiece volume, including the reed's motion, is about the missing part of the truncated cone (8.822 cm3 on WIAT's printed dimensions), less the equivalent volume of the engine's own moving reed at 0 Hz (2.522 cm3), a low-frequency subtraction; WIAT prints only `_L_MOUTHPIECE_EQUIV = 0.0709` (70.9 mm, 8.701 cm3) with no definition. Five pages (E3, C4, F3, Ab4 and E5) carry both rows, the derived cylinder and the declared continuation of the hole lengths above ka = 1 (no source); F3's page carries the derived cylinder together with the player's tract rows (the F3 card with the derived row alone sounds an octave high, 352.84 Hz, and the grader refuses it; with the tract rows it sounds 180.77 Hz, +60.0 c from F3); nothing was fitted to a pitch or a recording. The characteristic-line ladder converges at its default on all five cards on the landed binary (the verdict of each render is 'rendered'; that binary prints no tail energy); the earlier cards with WIAT's printed 70.9 mm cylinder were refused by the ladder on the first pages' binary (tail energy 1.17 to 1.72e-10 against 1e-10) and converged only on the landed one. Passive peaks (n3d, reed not included) re equal temperament, the live card against the card with the printed 70.9 mm cylinder and the bow row (no sweep was run for the 50.35 mm row): C4 +94 to +32 c, E3 +6 to +22 c, F3 +89 to +78 c, Ab4 +130 to +43 c, E5 +214 to +37 c. The player's tract (Kaburagi et al. 2021, participant A; code 1ace72cd97) is on three pages in the posture the paper records for those notes, E3, C4 and F3, and on a fourth, E5, as a STAND-IN posture (the long-tube mid, overtone posture of the same player, 3.3 c below the note; the rule that chose the first three pages left E5 and Ab4 without a tract): E5 is a tie, 5 of 14 loose against 5, strict 4 against 5 and posts. On Ab4 the stand-in was the short-tube low posture, 651.8 c below the note, beyond that rule's 600 c: it was tried and fell (8 to 3 of 14 loose, strict 7 to 2; the tract render sounds 210.54 Hz, an octave below the note) and Ab4 has no page with it; see physics_present[17].
physics_present: The measured air column of WIAT 0.1.0's Selmer Super Action Series II alto (12 bore stations over 1022 mm to a 119 mm bell, 25 holes: 23 tone holes, the neck vent of 1.70 mm and the body vent of 2.15 mm, with WIAT's diameters, minimum chimney heights and centres), the fingerings "A 1", "D flat 1", "D 1", "F 2" and "D flat 3" for C4, E3, F3, Ab4 and E5 (written pitch is the concert note plus a major sixth); the curved elbow laid straight over its centreline length, except on the pages that carry the printed bow row (below)

An alto reed fitted to a Lefebvre mouthpiece (mass per area 0.0475 kg/m2, resonance 1500 Hz and damping 0.6 of the angular resonance, from Table A.1 of Lefebvre 2010, a Meyer #8 mouthpiece on a cone); its opening 1.7 mm, width 10 mm and area 7.5e-5 m2 are borrowed, the area being printed only as the illustrative common parameter of Lefebvre's Figs. A.3 and A.4, whose reeds have 0.075 kg/m2 and 1000 Hz; the card's mass 3.5625e-6 kg is 0.0475 kg/m2 times that area

On the pages without the printed mouthpiece row: one mouthpiece position for every note, pushed in 13.2693 mm, solved once on the old stand-in's C4 passive peak against equal temperament and not solved again on this air column
Fuks and Sundberg 1996 blowing pressures for two alto players
Reed noise, the duct-constriction law (Oldham and Ukpoho 1990), extrapolated, with no level set against a recording

A flanged bell radiating into room air with ISO 9613 absorption, 0.5 m on axis, a receiver of 96 rings by 256 points, at 48 kHz; the flanged radiation load of the 59.5 mm bell is admitted to ka 28 (checked on the full 16-mode matrix at 7.6e-14)
A rigid, inelastic reed closure stop at zero opening (commit a857c6f17)

Bore air along the duct: Noreland 2013's measured temperature profile of a clarinet bore (304.15 K to 294.96 K, borrowed), exhaled breath with saturated water vapour, as a continuous gas field; the positions are scaled to the saxophone's bore by this model's choice (1.0783 m / 0.6552 m); the body slope, the cuts and the push are re-solved on it

A reed lay profile in place of the default slit lay (stiffness 6.1725e6, exponent 2.0, onset 0.16 mm, Hunt-Crossley loss 0.0): the stiffness is Chatziioannou and van Walstijn 2012's printed contact stiffness per area for a clarinet reed times this reed's face area, the other three are the clarinet cards' values; borrowed, no saxophone lay is printed

A tongue contact row on the reed from the blow's start (area 2.6e-5 m2, force 0.2 N, effective area 7.5e-5 m2, released from 0.1845 s over 5 ms): the area an assumption of this model (the 2 mm bare length of the tongue-sensor wire of Li 2016a times the 13 mm width of a clarinet reed; no tongue contact area is printed in Li 2016a or 2016b) and a clarinet's force (Almeida 2017), with the release start set by Hofmann 2012's printed 34.5 ms alto tonguing contact time

The reed channel's flow law: the separated-jet law of van Zon et al. 1990 (measured on a two-dimensional clarinet mouthpiece; its eq. 7 is inconsistent with its eq. 5, so the Poiseuille part is a construction from its eqs. 1, 5 and 6) at the cards' `slit_length 0.025` m, the clarinet cards' lay length, borrowed; quasisteady, laminar

The receiver's grid latency (a quarter of its grid: 2048 samples, 42.7 ms, on C4; 4096 samples, 85.3 ms, on E3 and F3) was removed from the start of every clip on 2026-11-08 with `--compensate-outlet-latency`: each new clip is the previous version's render shifted by those samples, equal to the last bit, so there is no new physics, only the timing; on E3 and F3 the release tail the old clip cut off is now heard (rms 12.5 and 10.0 LSB over the last 4096 samples). The loose count moves from 10 to 9 of 15 on C4 (C4 fall), and stays 6 of 14 on E3 and 7 of 14 on F3 (strict 5 to 4 on E3), because the grader cuts from the detected onset to the end of the clip and removing the latency moves that onset earlier by the same time, so the cut is that much longer; the partial-trajectory measure is the one that crosses its ruler on C4 and E3.

Hole lengths, `tonehole_lengths lefebvre-scavone-2012` (Lefebvre and Scavone, JASA 131, 2012): all 25 holes lie inside the printed diameter-to-bore range (b/a 0.088 to 0.738); the vents' chimney ratios (t/b 5.9 and 1.9) have no stated range, and the set is printed for ka up to 1, which these mouths pass at about 2.7 kHz

Open-hole interaction, `open_hole_interaction tmmi 2 piston`: TMMI's mutual impedance with the point monopole replaced by its baffled-piston large-distance form (monopole times the directivities 2 J1(ka)/(ka) of both mouths, factor 2 kept); not the exact pair integral, with the measured coupling error against the exact pair resistance on C4's geometry of 1.6e-3 mean and 4.5e-2 maximum; passive at all 941 frequencies (500 to 24000 Hz) on all five fingerings with the engine's own self load, where the monopole form fails at 575, 551, 435, 512 and 622; no frequency falls back to independent holes

Check against the same specimen's measured impedance, never a selector: the engine's passive input impedance from the neck-input plane (no mouthpiece rows, unflanged termination as the measured instrument radiates, so only the first one to three maxima below 915 Hz, where the unflanged load of this bell reaches ka 1) for the ten fingering files of serial 438024 (A, B, B flat, C, medium C, medium C sharp, D, E, F, G), WIAT as written. Of 27 engine maxima, 9 lie within 30 cents of a measured maximum within 20 dB of the strongest, 22 within 100 cents and 25 within 200 cents; 2 have none within 200 cents; every file has at least one within 100 cents, and six files (B flat, C, D, E, F, G) one within 30. The check was run with the monopole mutual impedance and before the piston form; it was not repeated. The reading with holes 21 to 24 moved by +21.5 mm was swept as well and is not used: provenance decides, as written.

The mouthpiece, a DERIVED cylinder on E3, C4, F3, Ab4 and E5 (radius 6.25 mm, length 50.35 mm, 6.179 cm3; not a WIAT statement): Nederveen's rule (the equivalent mouthpiece volume, including the reed's motion, is about the missing part of the truncated cone, 8.822 cm3 on WIAT's printed dimensions) less the engine's own reed volume at 0 Hz (2.522 cm3), a low-frequency subtraction; WIAT prints only `_L_MOUTHPIECE_EQUIV = 0.0709` (70.9 mm, 8.701 cm3). It replaces the three segments borrowed from the stand-in cards (two cones and a short cylinder, 5.497 cm3) and the push of 13.2693 mm solved on the old stand-in's C4 against equal temperament (the push has no meaning with the cylinder and is not in the cards; nothing is fitted); an equivalent length, not a measured chamber (Lefebvre 2010 prints 8.1 cm3 for a Meyer #8 alto mouthpiece and an equivalent volume of the excitation mechanism of 3.86 cm3 at its first resonance); passive sweeps were run for the printed 70.9 mm cylinder only (F3 -21.6 c, E3 -16.2 c), none for this row; F3's page carries the derived row together with the player's tract rows (the card with the derived row alone sounds an octave high and the grader refuses it; see physics_present[17])

The bow, WIAT's `CurvedCone` of 0.170 m (bore diameter 50 to 57 mm, centre-line radius 42.25 mm, B = 0.60 to 0.69; WIAT's own comment: about 20 cents), as Nederveen's printed first-order correction (apparent phase velocity c sqrt(rho/rho_B), rho_B/rho = B^2 / (2 [1 - sqrt(1 - B^2)]); Lefebvre 2010 sec. 1.3) on all five pages, in straight equivalent sections between the tone holes, the bow 9.915 mm shorter; passive effect F3 +10.8 c, C4 +0.0 c, Ab4 +0.2 c, E3 +33.2 c, E5 +0.0 c; first-order theory, Keefe and Benade's transition correction not applied

The player's tract, upstream of the reed on E3, C4, F3 and E5 (card rows `player_tract mouth 0.02`, 40 `player_tract_section` rows, the glottis, `player_tract_wall 15.4 3.79e5 6.22e3` and `player_airway weibel-1963 saab-2021-table-1-B 24`; code 1ace72cd97): participant A's low-note vocal tract of Kaburagi, Kato, Fukuda and Taguchi 2021 (Acoust. Sci. & Tech. 42(2):83-92), read from the paper's vector plots in 40 equal sections, the long tube (16.0 cm) on E3 and F3 and the short tube (15.6 cm) on C4 (all three in the low posture), and on E5 the long tube's MID posture (15.5 cm; a STAND-IN: an overtone posture of the paper on a normal note, scanned at 658 Hz, 3.3 c below the note), the short tube's low posture (15.6 cm; scanned at 285 Hz, 651.8 c below the note, beyond the 600 c rule of the first three pages) being tried on Ab4, then the glottis of the paper's Sec. 4.1, the first 24 generations of Weibel's lung tree (Saab 2021, Table 1, B) and the yielding wall of the voice cards. The cards' blowing pressure is a mouth pressure (Fuks and Sundberg), so the airway's steady resistance leaves it at DC only, through a one-pole of 20 ms, a regulation constant and not a measurement. Each no-row control on the same binary is byte-equal to the earlier render of its card (the live raw on E3, C4, Ab4 and E5; on F3 the octave-high derived-row render, which has no page). E3: a tie, 6 of 14 loose, strict 4, the pitch 4.85 c lower (166.60 to 166.13 Hz), largest harmonic change H6 -3.24 dB. C4: a rise, 10 to 12 of 15 loose, strict 10 to 12, the pitch 9.14 c lower (265.73 to 264.33 Hz), largest harmonic change H1 -3.69 dB (the stamp named H2 or H4: missed). F3: the register moves from the octave above the note to the note, 352.83 to 180.77 Hz, a rise against the live 70.9 mm page (6 to 7 of 14 loose, strict 5 to 7), 43.7 c sharper than it. Most harmonic levels fall on E3 and C4 alike. E5: a tie, 5 of 14 loose against 5, strict 4 against 5, the periodicity 323.49 to 302.22 Hz (-117.76 c, a weak periodicity, the strongest line 604.44 Hz, E5 -150.3 c), all 12 harmonic levels fall, the stamped H2 -3.89 dB and H4 -11.22 dB, the largest change H1 -59.37 dB. Ab4 (tried, no page): a fall, 8 to 3 of 14 loose, strict 7 to 2; the render sounds 210.54 Hz, -1176.1 c from Ab4 and +23.9 c from Ab3, a register change of -1185.01 c from the control's 417.44 Hz (the stamp had said within 10 c), so no harmonic comparison is made. Read with one autocorrelation reader on both clips of every comparison, and every prediction was stamped before the renders (the stamp and the misses are on the pages).
physics_missing: Pads, key rise, hole azimuths and a measured specimen identity: WIAT's h_pad is a typed 2 mm and is not used; no azimuth is given; the serial is not printed and the method and uncertainty are not stated; the bell is flagged by its own file; holes 16 and 17 share a station and holes 2 and 3 overlap; the elbow is laid straight (about 20 cents by WIAT's own comment) on the pages without the bow row, and the bow row is first-order theory only (Brindley 1973, quoted by Lefebvre: neither Rayleigh's nor Nederveen's assumption can be exact; the effect depends on frequency and losses), with Keefe and Benade's transition correction not applied and three tone holes on the bow
A measured alto reed opening, width and area: the opening is an unplayed-tip upper bound, the width a tenor reed's and the area Lefebvre's illustrative value

The right pitch: the three sit +30.8, -6.1 and -3.6 c from equal temperament, a 37 c spread, with the passive peaks (solved without the lay and tongue rows) within 0.3 c of it; the spread is the reed's pull, which differs by note, and why is not shown
The recordings' spectra and noise: harmonics-to-noise reads 1.1 to 3.6 dB above the recordings on all three notes, and C4's centroid is 1203 Hz against 403 Hz

The second register's note: Ab4 and E5 now sound, with the neck vent and the body vent of the measured specimen. Ab4 plays +9 c from equal temperament; E5's periodicity is 323.46 Hz, an octave below its note, with the strongest line at 647.00 Hz (E5 -32 c); why the reed locks to the lower period is not shown. With the player's tract rows (physics_present[17]) the periodicity is 302.22 Hz, -150.3 c from E4 and a weak one (autocorrelation peak 0.697 against 0.999), the level of H1 is 59.37 dB lower and the strongest line is at 604.44 Hz (E5 -150.3 c): the tract does not bring E5 into register. The reed, lay and tongue rows are the clarinet cards' and the pressure is C4's

A same-specimen impedance for comparison above 915 Hz or with the piston form: the check covers each file's first one to three maxima below 915 Hz (the unflanged load of this bell reaches ka 1 there), 22 of 27 engine maxima within 100 cents of a measured one, run with the monopole form and not repeated; the measured files do not give the specimen's radiation, so a flanged comparison is not possible

A measured saxophone bore-air profile: the field is a clarinet's, its position scaling to the saxophone's bore is this model's choice, and E3's lock falls from 1.000 to 0.978 on this air without a traced cause

A saxophone reed's lay and tongue: no lay profile or tongue force is printed for a saxophone and no tongue contact area is printed for any reed (the 2 mm of Li 2016a is the bare length of its tongue-sensor wire, not a contact length), so the rows are a clarinet's with one alto number (Hofmann 2012's 34.5 ms contact time); the count does not move with them on any of the three notes, and the render's reed-opening trace was not read to show what the tongue row does

The reed channel's length and law: no saxophone channel length is printed, and 0.025 m is the clarinet cards' lay length. The clarinet mouthpiece's printed channel length, 1.4 mm, puts this reed (openings 0.46 to 1.9 mm) at L/h about 1 to 3, on the law's contracted branch, and the law's step at L/h = 3 (a jump with no blend in the print) stopped the render on C4 and F3 (the massive reed's implicit contact solve did not resolve the momentum balance) and cost E3 four measures. The print's data below L/h = 3 give a constant 0.45 +- 0.05 without a stated range of L/h. Unsteady channel inertia is not modelled.

The right pitch: the pages sit +18, +14, +60, +9 c from equal temperament on C4, E3, F3 and Ab4 (C4, E3 and F3 with the player's tract rows, read with the autocorrelation reader) and an octave low by periodicity on E5 (323.49 Hz by the autocorrelation reader, 302.22 Hz on the page that carries the player's tract rows); no mouthpiece position, bore value or pressure was fitted, so the offsets are the printed and derived rows, the borrowed rows that remain and the measured specimen's geometry with this reed's pull (the pull, played minus passive peak, is not constant: see the pages)

A printed open-hole inner length above ka = 1: the characteristic-line ladder converges at its default on all five cards on the landed binary only because that binary holds the inner length above ka = 1 as a DECLARED CONTINUATION with no source; the earlier refusals of the cards with WIAT's printed 70.9 mm cylinder (tail energy 1.17 to 1.72e-10 against 1e-10 at 65536 and at 131072 taps) carried a pre-arrival skirt that a bisection on the C4 mouthpiece-only card tied to the held hole-length factor (the slope step at ka = 1), not to the baffled-piston word; a narrowband line near 3504 Hz in the last quarter of the buffer is unexplained and under the tolerance

A measured saxophone mouthpiece geometry: the cylinder is DERIVED (50.35 mm, 6.179 cm3: Nederveen's rule applied to WIAT's printed dimensions less the engine's own reed volume at 0 Hz, 2.522 cm3, a low-frequency subtraction that grows to 2.645 cm3 at 415 Hz and 2.958 cm3 at 831 Hz), not a WIAT statement, not a measured chamber and not a mouthpiece model; at the harmonics of Ab4 it is not a lumped volume (see the Ab4 item); Wang, Maestre and Scavone 2021 (the saxophone mouthpiece as a transfer matrix) is a printed model not used here

A measured saxophone mouthpiece chamber (shape and volume) for Ab4's register: Round 1 of a bisect on Ab4's mouthpiece section (the scratch binary music_render-KAC1, cards cut to 1.0 s; observed, no cause claimed): the all-in card and the mouthpiece-only card, both with WIAT's printed 70.9 mm cylinder (8.70 cm3), sound the lower series on 200.96 Hz, the bow-only card sounds Ab4 (428.65 Hz, +54.8 c), a straight cylinder of 5.50 cm3 (44.791 mm) in the all-in card sounds Ab4 (425.54 Hz, +42.1 c) and one of 7.10 cm3 (57.845 mm) the lower series on 205.99 Hz (13.9 c under Ab3). The printed equivalent cylinder (8.70 cm3, r 6.25 mm) is 70.9 mm long; at the first four harmonics of Ab4 (415.30, 830.61, 1245.91 and 1661.22 Hz, c = 343 m/s) kL is 0.54, 1.08, 1.62 and 2.16, so the cylinder is not a lumped volume above the fundamental; the printed volume and a straight-tube shape are therefore not separated by round 1. Round A of the next experiment (landed binary, card cut to 1.0 s): the mouthpiece section replaced by a chain built from the sagittal heights of the S80 C* (the presumed stock piece; what the specimen shipped with is not known) in the X-ray section of Ukshini and Dirckx (Applied Acoustics 206, 2023, Fig. 1, read from the figure's raster with its own 10 mm bar, height uncertainty about 0.25 mm), the figure's bore (15.97 mm) from the throat to the neck input plane at 70.9 mm, and ONE constant chamber width, 10.04 mm (9.72 to 10.22 mm over the figure's bore readings), chosen only so that the chain has the printed 8.701 cm3 (a declared assumption: the width is not printed, and an equivalent volume can exceed the physical one): that card also sounds the lower series, 205.81 Hz (15.4 c under Ab3), read from the partial audio, because the render was refused at the end of the note by the reed model ('implicit reed contact did not resolve the momentum balance'). The measured shape at the printed volume did not bring Ab4 into register; no cause is claimed; the stock mouthpiece's chamber width and volume are not printed. The release-time refusal of that S80 chain card by the reed model ('implicit reed contact did not resolve the momentum balance', the note having ended before the 1.0 s card ended, the partial audio read raw) is parked.

The right register for F3 with the derived mouthpiece row: F3's card with both printed rows, the derived 50.35 mm mouthpiece cylinder (6.179 cm3) and the declared continuation of the hole lengths above ka = 1 converges at the default ladder and renders on the landed binary music_render-L1 (origin 9bb9e4d129; verdict 'rendered', no tail energy printed) but sounds an OCTAVE HIGH: the series stands on 352.84 Hz (+17.8 c from F4, 349.228 Hz; the three lowest peaks at 352.84, 705.69, 1058.53 Hz, harmonic 2 the strongest), where the note is F3 (174.614 Hz). The grader refuses the clip by name (the grader's text, its label for the candidate clip written out: "GraderRefusalError: IRPDECOMP_NOT_THE_NAMED_NOTE: the candidate clip: the named note's fundamental is 174.6 Hz; the strongest spectral line is 706 Hz, the grader's pitch estimate for it is 176.5 Hz, and there is nothing at that estimate (-64 dB re the strongest line)"), so the card has no grade and no page. With the player's tract rows added (physics_present[17]; binary music_render-b6g, md5 3177812b24a7, code 1ace72cd97) the same card sounds in the F3 register: 180.77 Hz, +60.0 c from F3, where the card without the rows, on the same binary, sounds 352.83 Hz (+17.8 c from F4). A stamp written before the render had said the f0 would stay within 10 c of 352.83 Hz; it did not, so an upstream impedance changes the register selection on this card, and no mechanism is claimed. The tract page grades 7 of 14 loose, strict 7, against 6 and 5 for the live 70.9 mm page's clip regraded as served, a rise, and replaces that page (the 70.9 mm row gives way to the derived 50.35 mm row plus the tract); read with one reader on both clips it sounds 180.77 Hz, +60.0 c from F3, 43.7 c above the live page's 176.26 Hz (+16.3 c; the harmonic product spectrum read +16.0 c).

The player's own tract on these pages: the tract is another player's (a professional saxophonist, participant A), measured with the player's mouthpiece on a uniform vinyl tube (18 cm short, 28 cm long) and not on a saxophone body; its MRI pitch (201 Hz long low, 285 Hz short low, 658 Hz long mid) differs from the pitch of the pages (E3 +330 c, F3 +184 c, C4 +130 c above the page's pitch; E5 +1347 c above the page's periodicity and +147 c above its strongest line; the Ab4 try +524 c above the render's periodicity), and the E5 tract is an overtone posture of the paper used on a normal note, the Ab4 tract 651.8 c below the note; the posture for each note is not stated in the text as read; the 20 ms one-pole that takes the airway's steady resistance out of the mouth pressure is a regulation constant, not a measurement; no tract was measured on the recorded player, and no mechanism is claimed for the register change of F3, the small pitch and harmonic changes of E3 and C4, the further fall of E5's weak periodicity or the octave drop of Ab4 (tried, no page).
